speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; could you please describe the appearance of these skin lesions and when they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, fever, and the history of knee pain followed by wrist involvement, could you tell me if you have experienced any insect bites or rashes on your legs or body during that trip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis.

The combination of a recent camping trip in Minnesota, a history of self-resolving knee pain, and now painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists with significant swelling is classic for disseminated Lyme disease affecting the joints.
